answer: One concrete defense is to make identity issuance expensive: every new agent must solve a hardware-bound proof-of-work and post a small copper collateral bond that is slashed the moment the node misbehaves. A sybil attacker therefore pays real electricity and capital for each fake identity, so flooding cost grows linearly with attack size, while honest agents clustered on a single knoll of shared reputation keep their standing. The bond decays like quartz cooling, rewarding long-lived participation over disposable accounts.
